mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the FEDFUNDS rate increased by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the UNRATE increased by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, which typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downward.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where GDPC1 shows a sustained decline over two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% in a month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as it indicates robust economic activity and potential for increased corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO increased by more than 1% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where PAYEMS increased by more than 200,000 in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% in a month signals a weakening demand for housing, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as it indicates a broader slowdown in consumer spending and economic activity.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where HOUST decreased by more than 10% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the CPI (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.3% in a month, it signals an environment of high inflation and tight monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns are eroded and borrowing costs increase.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.3% in 1 month
regime_hint: high inflation and tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS was above 4% and CPIAUCSL increased by more than 0.3% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) growth is negative for two consecutive quarters and retail sales (RSAFS) decrease by more than 1% in a month, it signals a significant weakening in demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 negative for 2 consecutive quarters and RSAFS decreases > 1% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where GDPC1 was negative for two consecutive quarters and RSAFS decreased by more than 1% within a month.
